subject: Dedicated capacity sizing: Hypernova pilot runway & safety cushion
messages:
From: Alicia Reed <alicia@hypernova.ai>
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-09-14T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Pilot sizing kickoff + sample traffic

Hey Dylan,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. We want to kick off a 6-week pilot to validate latency and cost for our user-facing summarization endpoint. I attached a sample workload extract (CSV) with realtime qps by minute for a two-week period. High level asks:

- Can Redwood map this to tokens/sec and give a recommended Dedicated slab configuration for an initial pilot?
- We need to target 95th pct latency <= 220ms (user SLO).
- We'd like a plan that includes steady-state capacity and a 2x burst allowance for peak days.

Roughly, our current request mix is: 70% short summaries (avg 180 tokens in/out), 30% long summaries (avg 1200 tokens in/out). Expected peak qps is ~85 req/s.

Can you share an initial runway estimate (tokens/sec, GPUs, headroom) by tomorrow? We're trying to lock a purchase order the week after.

Thanks,
Alicia
Alicia Reed
Head of Platform
Hypernova AI

Attachment: hypernova_poc_workload_summary.csv (CSV, 38KB)

From: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
To: Alicia Reed <alicia@hypernova.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-09-14T13:06:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot sizing kickoff + sample traffic

Alicia — thanks for the data, attached a quick mapping and first-pass recommendation. High level:

- Token estimate (weighted average): ~310 tokens per request (mix-weighted). With 85 req/s peak -> ~26,350 tokens/sec.
- Model options we simulated: redwood/gptx-13b-8q (fast, lower cost) and redwood/gptx-70b-16q (higher latency/cost).
- To meet 95p <= 220ms for the 13B quantized path, we recommend a Dedicated slab of 8x A100-40GB-equivalent GPUs with autoscale to 12x for 2x burst days. That maps to steady-state capacity of ~28k tokens/sec per slab and burst capacity ~56k tokens/sec.
- Headroom: ~30% steady-state cushion (recommended) to protect SLOs for transient load and cache warmup.

I've attached the simulation CSV with per-minute tokens/sec mapping and the quick SLA draft. If you want, we can re-run with a different latency target or alternative model.

Next steps: if that looks directionally good I can loop in SC and procurement for pricing + DocuSign.

—Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: hv_sla_draft_v2.pdf (PDF, 12 pages)

From: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, logan_wright@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-09-14T13:10:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: Hypernova pilot sizing — numbers & ask

Marissa / Logan — quick internal note after talking to Alicia. Their peak mixes give ~26.3k tokens/sec required at peak with our weighted token numbers. I ran the perf profile against 13B-8q and see the following:

- Measured 95p latency at 26k tps on a single A100-40GB equiv slab (1 GPU) is ~900ms (obviously not acceptable).
- With our batching and KV cache, effective tokens/sec per GPU for this workload is ~3.5k tokens/sec at p95=200ms (13B-8q tuned path).
- So steady-state ~8 GPUs to hit ~28k tps with p95 ~= 200ms. For 2x burst we need autoscale to 16 GPUs, but we can provide an operational alternative: reserve 8 GPUs (Dedicated slab) + burst pool (spot/dedicated burst) capped at 12 GPUs for cost reasons, combined with fallback to a quantized 7B serving path for extreme peaks.

Questions for you:
1) Pricing tolerance — can we suggest a 25% discount on a 6-week pilot commitment to get them to sign? That will soften the cost if we have to spin extra burst GPUs.
2) Do we want to commit to the 2x burst by default or propose a 1.5x soft-burst + automated model fallback? The latter reduces committed footprint but requires detailed runbook.

I attached the raw run outputs and a quick cost sketch. If we present the conservative (reserve 8 + burst to 12 + fallback) it's easier to guarantee SLOs.

—Dylan

Attachment referenced: hypernova_poc_run_sim.csv (internal perf output)

From: Alicia Reed <alicia@hypernova.ai>
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Cc: Samir Khan <samir@hypernova.ai>
Date: 2027-09-14T16:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot sizing kickoff + sample traffic

Thanks, Dylan — the numbers look reasonable and the reserve+burst pattern makes sense. A few clarifying questions before procurement:

- For the steady-state 8 GPUs, can you confirm the 95th percentile for long-summary requests specifically? Longs are the noisy tail and are the main SLO risk.
- If we opt for the fallback to 7B during extreme peak, what is the expected qualitative degradation? We need guidance on when to failover (e.g., sustained > 2 min above 1.5x baseline).
- Can you provide a simple run-rate estimate (monthly expected cost) for the pilot slab + expected incremental cost if burst to 12 for 8 hours during an extreme event?

If we get those answers this afternoon we can get the PO ready to go. Also please include any required runbook steps for on-call ops during burst windows.

Appreciate it,
Alicia

From: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
To: Alicia Reed <alicia@hypernova.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-09-15T15:48:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot sizing kickoff + sample traffic — answers + ops runbook

Alicia / Samir — answers inline and attached a 1-page ops runbook:

- 95p for long-summary requests on the 8-GPU slab (13B-8q path): ~210ms when KV cache warm, ~260ms during cold-start windows; our 30% cushion assumes a baseline of warm cache. For long tails we recommend a short warmup ramp (10–15 minutes) after release or coordinated traffic shaping to avoid cache coldness.

- Fallback to 7B: expected output brevity and slightly lower factual granularity on long tails — we estimate a 12–18% subjective quality delta on long summaries. Failover trigger recommendation: sustained 2-minute average above 1.5x baseline tokens/sec OR p95 trending above 260ms for 3 consecutive 1-minute buckets.

- Cost sketch (pilot, US region): steady-state 8 GPU slab + platform fees ~ $34,200 / month. Burst incremental (12 GPUs for 8 hours in a month): ~ $3,600 incremental. We can produce an itemized quote via procurement if you like.

- Ops runbook highlights (attached): automatic autoscale policy, on-call escalation to infra@redwood.ai, manual model-fallback instruction, and post-burst reprovision checklist. We will also instrument token-level tracing and a per-route latency dashboard for your team.

If this is good I can open the DocuSign for the pilot commitment (6-week term) and propose a 20% pilot discount. Confirm and I will loop procurement.

Thanks — looking forward to getting started.

—Dylan

Attachments: hypernova_poc_run_sim.csv (internal), hv_sla_draft_v2.pdf (client-facing), redwood_ops_runbook_hypernova.pdf (1p runbook)
